metaTitle: Mercedes-AMG Performance Engine Rebuild | Mercedes Garage
metaDescription: Specialist performance engine rebuild for Mercedes-AMG V8 and 4-cylinder engines. Hand-built precision, tighter tolerances, dyno testing, and AMG-specific expertise.
lede: Precision rebuilds for AMG engines – M156, M157, M177, M178, M139, and more. Tighter tolerances, performance-grade parts, and full dyno validation to restore or enhance factory power.

sections.heading: What Sets AMG Engine Rebuilds Apart

steps.title: Tighter Tolerances
steps.body: AMG engines are assembled to finer clearances than standard Mercedes units. From crank journals to cylinder bores, every dimension must be measured and machined to AMG OE specifications.

steps.title: Specialised Components
steps.body: Unique valvetrain (e.g., M156's bucket tappets, M178's twin-scroll turbos), high-pressure fuel systems, and performance cooling and lubrication systems require specific expertise.

steps.title: Precision Machining
steps.body: Cylinder bores, deck surfaces, and crank journals must be finished to tighter roughness and roundness specs. We use CNC-controlled machining and AMG-specified tooling.

steps.title: Rigorous Testing
steps.body: Every AMG rebuild is run on an engine dynamometer under load, including break-in cycles and high-RPM verification. We check oil pressure, fuel delivery, and power output against factory baselines.

paras: AMG engines require higher-grade parts and more labour – our rebuilds start at: **£6,500 for AMG V8 (M156/M157/M177/M178)** AMG 4-cylinder (M139) from £3,600

blocks.html: Pricing includes full disassembly, machining, replacement of all wear parts with genuine or OE-spec components, assembly, and dynamometer testing.
We cover the full range of Mercedes-AMG performance engines – from the M139 4-cylinder to the M178 V8 and everything in between.

items.label: AMG GT (GT, GT S, GT R, GT 63)

steps.title: Complete Strip-Down
steps.body: We disassemble the engine to the bare block. Every component is labelled, inspected, and measured against AMG OE tolerances.

steps.title: Precision Machining
steps.body: Cylinder bores are honed to the correct cross-hatch pattern, crankshaft journals are polished, and deck surfaces are checked for flatness. All machining is done to AMG-specified tolerances.

steps.title: Replace All Wear Parts
steps.body: We use genuine or OE-spec performance parts: timing chains, tensioners, guides, bearings, piston rings, valve stem seals, and gaskets. For AMG engines, we also replace turbocharger seals and coolant components where needed.

steps.title: Assembly with AMG Torque Specifications
steps.body: Each bolt is torqued to AMG's specific values, using angle-tightening where required. We use AMG-specified sealants and assembly lubricants.

steps.title: Engine Dynamometer Testing
steps.body: The rebuilt engine is run on a dyno under load. We perform break-in cycles, check oil pressure, fuel delivery, ignition timing, and verify power output against baseline data.

steps.title: Final Installation & Road Test
steps.body: After dyno approval, the engine is installed in the vehicle, road-tested, and subjected to a final diagnostic check with Mercedes-Star Diagnostic (Xentry).

sections.heading: Is an AMG Performance Rebuild Right for You?

steps.title: 1. Engine assessment
steps.body: We inspect your AMG engine – compression, leak-down, oil analysis – to determine the scope of work needed. Many AMG engines benefit from a full rebuild after 80,000-100,000 miles.

steps.title: 2. Custom rebuild plan
steps.body: We create a tailored rebuild plan covering all wear items, machining, and any upgrades you may want (e.g., stronger head studs, upgraded turbocharger components).

steps.title: 3. Precision rebuild & testing
steps.body: We carry out the rebuild with our in-house machining and dyno testing, ensuring the engine performs to AMG standards.

steps.title: 4. Installation & warranty
steps.body: We install the engine, road-test the vehicle, and provide a 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty for your peace of mind.

items.q: What AMG engines do you rebuild?
items.a: We rebuild all AMG engines: M156 (6.2L V8), M157 (5.5L V8 twin-turbo), M177/M178 (4.0L V8 twin-turbo), M159 (6.2L V8, SLS), and M139 (4-cylinder turbo). We also rebuild older AMG V12 engines (M275) on request.

items.q: How is an AMG rebuild different from a standard Mercedes rebuild?
items.a: AMG engines require tighter tolerances, higher-grade materials, and more precise machining. The assembly process is more labour-intensive, and we use AMG-specific torque sequences and sealants. Post-rebuild testing is performed on a dynamometer under high load to validate performance.

items.q: Do you address known AMG-specific issues during the rebuild?
items.a: Yes. For M156 engines (pre-2012), we replace camshaft adjusters and upgrade head bolts. For M157/M177 engines, we replace valve stem seals and coolant system components as part of our standard rebuild procedure, addressing known wear patterns.

items.q: What parts are replaced during an AMG rebuild?
items.a: We replace timing chains, tensioners, guides, bearings, piston rings, valve stem seals, gaskets, oil pump components, and any worn turbocharger or ancillary parts. We use genuine Mercedes-AMG or OE-spec performance parts exclusively.

items.q: How long does an AMG rebuild take?
items.a: Typically 3-5 working days for disassembly, machining, parts procurement, assembly, and dyno testing. Complex builds with custom parts may take longer – we'll give you a precise timeline when you enquire.

items.q: What warranty do you offer on AMG rebuilds?
items.a: Our AMG rebuilds come with a 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty covering parts and labour for any workmanship or component defects.
